title: Preset allocation mapper — labnotes
content:
Purpose and quick context:

This is a messy scratchpad for the idea I started sketching in the whiteboard session on 2025-08-12: a small service that maps high-level user-facing 'presets' (Quality / Cost / Privacy) to concrete runtime allocations and config bits (GPU class, quant profile, batch hints, KV cache TTL, fallback variant). The aim is to:
- reduce repeated scaffolding in product code when offering user-configurable performance tiers
- centralize mapping so rollout changes to presets don't require code changes everywhere
- provide an API for both the Console and SDKs to request a resolved runtime profile

Design goals (non-exhaustive):
- deterministic: same preset + tenant + route => same resolved profile unless explicitly versioned
- traceable: store the mapping decisions and reasons for each resolution for debugging/observability
- incremental: presets can inherit/compose other presets (eg "high-throughput" inherits "default" and overrides batch_size)
- safe fallback: when a requested allocation is unavailable, return a chain of fallback variants with cost/latency estimates

High-level API shape (sketch):
POST /v1/presets/resolve
Request body:
{
  "tenant_id": "string",
  "route": "string",             // e.g. /v1/generate-chat
  "preset": "string",           // e.g. fast-low-cost / private-high
  "max_latency_ms": 350,         // optional hint
  "tokens_estimate": 200,        // optional for cost-ranking
  "context_features": ["kv-warm:mmr=0.8"]  // optional hints from client telemetry
}

Response (resolver output):
{
  "profile_id": "preset-resolve:v2025-08-14:a1",
  "model_variant": "vicuna-13b-q4_onnx",
  "gpu_target": "a10g-rtx",
  "quant_profile": "q4-dynamic",
  "batch_hint": { "preferred": 8, "max": 32 },
  "kv_cache": { "enabled": true, "ttl_s": 600 },
  "estimated_latency_ms": 120,
  "estimated_cost_per_1k_tokens_usd": "0.0042",
  "fallback_chain": ["vicuna-13b-q4_onnx", "llama-7b-q4_cpu_fuse"],
  "resolution_trace_id": "rslv-03f2c",
  "notes": "inherited 'fast' preset, disabled vector-sparse-quant due to tenant opt-out"
}

Config schema sketch (YAML-ish, internal representation):
presets:
  default:
    model_variant: "vicuna-13b"
    quant_profile: "q4"
    batch_hint: { preferred: 4, max: 16 }
    kv_cache: { enabled: true, ttl_s: 300 }
    route_overrides: {}

  fast-low-cost:
    inherits: [default]
    model_variant: "vicuna-13b-q4_onnx"
    gpu_target: "a10g-rtx"
    batch_hint: { preferred: 8, max: 32 }
    kv_cache: { enabled: true, ttl_s: 120 }
    fallbacks: ["llama-7b-q4_cpu_fuse"]

  private-high:
    inherits: [default]
    model_variant: "vicuna-13b-int8_secure"
    quant_profile: "int8_secure"
    gpu_target: "p4d-secure"
    kv_cache: { enabled: false }  # privacy constraint

Notes on resolution logic (brain dump):
- Merge order: global defaults <- preset inheritance chain (left-to-right) <- tenant policy overrides <- route-specific overrides <- runtime availability patching
- Tenant policies can tag tenants with 'no-int8' or 'no-shared-kv' which the resolver must respect.
- When availability check fails (e.g., no a10g in region), the resolver consults the 'fallback_chain' field and returns the first compatible variant with a best-effort latency estimate.
- Versioning: each preset config change increments a v-tag (profile_id) so historical requests can be reproduced for debugging and evals.

Operational/observability hooks I want:
- Emit an event for each resolution: { resolution_trace_id, preset, tenant, route, resolved_model, cost_estimate, why_fell_back }
- Store resolution decisions in short-term store (7d) + long-term sampling for regressions
- Expose /v1/presets/validate to run "what-if" for a tenant and set of signals

ASCII diagram (conceptual):

client (Console/SDK) -> preset-resolver -> availability-check -> runtime-router -> serving-runtime\                                              |
                                              v
                                            kv-config-store (ttl/policy)

Key implementation questions / things to try:
- Should resolver be synchronous low-latency (50ms) or allow async warm-up + caching with a synchronous cache key? I think both: cache the resolved profile per tenant+route+preset and fall back to on-demand resolution when cache miss.
- How to surface cost/latency estimates? Keep simple heuristics first (tokens_estimate * per_model_token_cost) and refine later with telemetry models.
- How to handle canarying presets? Idea: add 'rollout' key in preset config with weight and tenant selector; resolver returns candidate list with weights when in canary mode.

Small TODOs (actionable):
- [ ] write minimal proto for resolve API (input+output) and push to github/preset-service
- [ ] prototype resolver in python using in-memory config and naive availability checker
- [ ] add resolution event schema to tracing team backlog
- [ ] sketch Console UX for "presets" with a slider mapping to these preset names (Marcel to pick up)

Open questions for the team (call out in PR):
- What is the authoritative source of 'model_variant' capability attributes (quant support, memory footprint)? Current thought: model-catalog service owns this and exposes a simple capability set the resolver queries.
- Do we let product teams create arbitrary presets in Console or limit to typed templates? Risk: explosion of presets that make SLOs hard to guarantee.

Random experiment notes (from playing on laptop):
- q4_onnx variants behave poorly on sequences > 4k with current runtime kernel; fallback selection for long-context routes must consider sequence profile as first-class signal.
- TTL of KV cache at 120s seems ok for chat UX, but increases miss rate in bursty sessions. Consider adaptive ttl based on "session-hotness" metric.

If this resonates I can turn it into a quick 1-pager that includes a minimal data model (DB table for profile cache + trace), and a proto/HTTP spec for the /resolve endpoint. For now leaving as a mess of thoughts so I can come back and expand after prototyping.

----
Sign-off: Asha (quick personal labnotes)
